description: A horizontally scalable, Jellyfin-compatible video server in Go. Every task below comes from PRODUCT.md (features and roadmap), the project plan, compat/coverage-12.4.tsv and the agreed work queue. PRODUCT.md stays the source of truth for status; update this file when a slice merges.

conventions.status: done | in_progress | todo; passes is true only when done
conventions.priority: 1 is next; done tasks have none
conventions.delivery: each task goes through the build workflow (.claude/workflows/build.js): checks written first and locked, one implementer until they pass, QA and one blind adversarial review with evidence-gated findings, one fix round; then PR, CI, merge, redeploy the dogfood
conventions.differential: a task that adds or changes a route jellyfin-web or another client calls adds its requests to test/differential/requests.yaml, and any difference it keeps to compat/differences.yaml with a reason

userStories.description: Report VideoRange and VideoRangeType as Jellyfin 12.4 does (DOVI for P5, DOVIWithEL for P7, DOVIWithHDR10, DOVIWithHLG and DOVIWithSDR for P8 by base-layer compatibility, HDR10Plus and the DOVI-with-HDR10+ variants), stop stripping them from client DTOs, and use them in the playback decision: a client whose profile allows HDR10 (or HLG, or SDR) but not Dolby Vision plays a DV file whose base layer it supports, instead of a re-encode.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed against a real Jellyfin 12.4 first (synthetic DV fixtures in a disposable jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 container): item DTOs, PlaybackInfo decisions and the master playlist's codec tag for P5, P7 and P8.1; capture in compat/captures
The scan records the DV profile, base-layer compatibility id and HDR10+ presence
Item and PlaybackInfo DTOs carry VideoRange and VideoRangeType for SDR, HDR10, HDR10Plus, HLG and each DV variant

A profile that allows HDR10 but no DOVI type direct plays or copies a P8.1 file as HDR10; one that allows nothing HDR re-encodes with tone mapping as today; P5 (no compatible base layer) is never sent to a client without DV
The decision table tests cover every VideoRangeType against jellyfin-web's own profile conditions
Checked on the dogfood with a P8.1 film and a P7 film in jellyfin-web and one TV client
userStories.source: work queue 4; internal/library/scan.go strips them today
userStories.notes: Found while preparing the task (2026-11-07): Jellyfin's labels drive decisions, not only display. jellyfin-web sends CodecProfiles conditions on VideoRangeType, and Jellyfin copies a DOVIWithHDR10 stream to an HDR10-only client (tagging it db1p in the master playlist). jellyscale reports every DV file as plain DOVI, so those films are re-encoded in software today.

Three worker processes encode one film in chunks; the assembled segments equal a single worker's video byte for byte

A helper killed mid-chunk is replaced and the viewer keeps playing

userStories.title: Differential compatibility tier against a real Jellyfin 12.4
userStories.description: Run jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 and jellyscale side by side over the same fixtures, replay the same requests to both, and diff normalized responses (JSON with ids, timestamps and ordering normalized; headers; HLS playlists). Intentional improvements on Jellyfin go in an allowlist with a reason each. This is the project plan's jfdiff, never built.
acceptanceCriteria: A test tier starts a disposable Jellyfin 12.4 on a Docker-assigned port over the e2e fixtures and diffs every route the tier knows

Shows the Continue Reading bug of PR #32 as a diff when the fix is reverted
Runs in CI (sharded if needed) and locally; docs/testing.md explains adding a route
Later compatibility tasks can state acceptance as 'route X matches, apart from the allowlist'
userStories.notes: Evidence: agents converge when they can loop against a known-good reference (Anthropic's C compiler diffed against GCC; Ladybird's LibJS port held byte-identical output and passed 52,898 test262 tests; Airbnb and Google migrations verified every step). Compatibility with unmodified clients is jellyscale's top risk, and today it is checked only by hand-made captures and jellyfin-web in Playwright.

userStories.title: Lease and failover invariant tests under fault injection
userStories.description: Property-style tests with real processes over randomized schedules: kill a worker mid-lease, restart Postgres, pause a worker (SIGSTOP), slow the database; assert at most one owner per job, no job lost, and resumption within the stated bound; a soak mode for flake hunting.
acceptanceCriteria: Each invariant (single owner, no lost job, resume bound, no segment stored by a dead owner) has a test that fails when the guarding code is removed
Randomized schedules with a printed seed that reproduces a failure
A soak mode (many repetitions) documented in docs/testing.md and run before failover changes merge
userStories.notes: Evidence: tests block regressions where review comments do not (Anthropic's C compiler: CI stopped new features breaking old ones; agentic property-based testing found real bugs, 86% valid among top-ranked reports).

userStories.title: Harden the differential tier
userStories.description: JS-064's review backlog, closed before later tasks lean on the tier. A request meant to return rows asserts 200 and a non-empty answer, so a fixture or route broken on both servers can't pass. Timestamps are masked only where they change from run to run (DateCreated, LastPlayedDate, session times), so PremiereDate and similar stable dates are compared. A pinned (ids) entry that no longer matches fails, and is no longer reported as stale. acceptance.sh runs from a git-archive export, and its leak check counts only the containers of its own runs.
acceptanceCriteria: A request marked as returning rows fails the tier when both servers answer an error or an empty list, shown by a test
A wrong PremiereDate on jellyscale fails the tier; masked timestamp keys are listed in one place and documented
A pinned entry whose list changed fails without a contradictory 'no longer differs' note
acceptance.sh passes from a git-archive export and is not failed by a concurrent run.sh on the same host
userStories.source: JS-064 review backlog (QA and adversarial, build workflow 2026-11-07)
userStories.notes: Every later protocol task loops against this tier, so a false pass here is costly.

userStories.title: Client SDK conformance: the fields and checks SDK clients enforce
userStories.description: Findroid failed twice on the dogfood (2026-11-08) where jellyfin-web worked. First, jellyfin-sdk-kotlin's server discovery rejects any ProductName but "Jellyfin Server" (#44). Second, its strict decoder throws on a missing non-null field: four were missing from the sign-in response (#47), so Findroid reported bad credentials. The differential tier had seen two of them and filed them as a gap. Make the tier and CI enforce what client SDKs enforce: (1) derive, from a pinned jellyfin-sdk-kotlin release, the required (non-null, no default) fields of each response model, and fail the differential tier when a jellyscale response lacks one for its route's return type; (2) refuse an allowlist entry that hides a missing required field; (3) add the requests every client makes before its home screen to requests.yaml: /System/Info/Public, /System/Ping, /Users/Public, /Branding/Configuration, /QuickConnect/Enabled, sign-in itself, /Sessions, DisplayPreferences; (4) run @jellyfin/sdk's server discovery (TypeScript, as Streamyfin uses it) against jellyscale in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: The required fields per response model come from a pinned jellyfin-sdk-kotlin release by a script, not by hand, and the list is checked in with its version

The differential tier fails when a jellyscale response lacks a field the SDK requires for that route's return type, and an allowlist entry for such a field is refused; shown with ProductName and the four sign-in fields of #44 and #47 put back
requests.yaml covers the startup, discovery and sign-in requests above, and the tier passes
@jellyfin/sdk's recommended-server discovery accepts jellyscale in CI, and fails with ProductName put back
userStories.source: escaped defects from the dogfood, Findroid, 2026-11-08 (#44, #47)
userStories.notes: jellyfin-web ignores fields it doesn't read, so it can't catch this class; Kotlin and Swift SDK clients decode strictly. Scheduled after the web-client work (user, 2026-11-08: focus on the web client first, then pivot to other clients). Findroid's first home-screen call, GET /Items/Suggestions, 404s; a parked implementation is on branch feat/items-suggestions.
